title: Lebanese Chicken Shish Platter
seoTitle: Lebanese Chicken Shish Platter | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Garlic-lemon chicken skewers with toum and tabbouleh for ten
subtitle: Garlic-lemon chicken skewers with toum and tabbouleh for ten
description: Chicken breast chunks marinate in lemon, garlic, yogurt, and olive oil, then grill on skewers until charred at the edges. Serve with toum garlic sauce, tabbouleh, pickles, and warm pita.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.instruction: Mix lemon juice, olive oil, yogurt, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken and marinate at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Make toum
steps.instruction: Blend garlic with lemon juice, then slowly stream in oil until thick and fluffy like mayonnaise.

steps.title: Prep tabbouleh
steps.instruction: Soak bulgur in hot water 20 minutes, drain, and toss with parsley, diced tomato, cucumber, mint, lemon, and olive oil.

steps.title: Grill skewers
steps.instruction: Thread chicken onto skewers. Grill over medium-high heat 10–12 minutes until charred and 165°F internal. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Platter and serve
steps.instruction: Arrange skewers on platters with tabbouleh, toum, pickles, and warm pita. Slide chicken off skewers at the line if preferred.

proTips: Sumac on finished chicken adds classic Lebanese tang.
Pickled turnips from a jar are worth buying for authenticity.
If toum breaks, blend in another egg white to re-emulsify.
tonightSpread: Shish taouk with toum, tabbouleh, pickles, and warm pita.
Hummus on the side for double-dip energy.
leftovers: Chicken in pita with toum and pickles for lunch.
Tabbouleh holds 2 days—good side for next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shish taouk is Mediterranean comfort without the pasta or rice-bowl rut. Garlic-lemon chicken on skewers feels like a backyard cookout with better seasoning, and toum separates the rookies from crews who respect raw garlic.
mealPrepNotes: Yogurt marinade tenderizes breast meat—do not skip. Make toum in a food processor ahead. Tabbouleh improves if parsley is chopped fine and salad rests 30 minutes.
